newsitem.title: USA: W. Virginia settles last investment loss lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: W. Virginia settles last investment loss lawsuit.

text.p: Chase Securities Inc., a unit of Chemical Banking Group, has agreed to pay $6.65 million to West Virginia to settle the last lawsuit stemming from the state's 1987 investment losses, state officials said Wednesday.
Officials at Chase were not immediately available for comment.
West Virginia Managing Deputy Attorney General Silas Taylor said the firm did not admit any wrongdoing.
The state Board of Investments voted to accept the settlement Wednesday, executive director Jerry Simpson said.
"Thank goodness. In April we'll be coming up on our 10th anniversary of litigation," Simpson said.

West Virginia accused nine Wall Street brokerage firms of misleading state officials after the state lost $279 million in its pooled investment fund in 1987. The state claimed that the investments, which included Treasury-based derivatives, were unsuitably risky for public funds and were made in violation of state investment guidelines.

"Based on the (recorded) trade conversations, it was felt that our people who were in charge of the investment activity at that time were misled as to the type of investments they were doing and the appropriateness of it," Simpson said.
Seven firms agreed to pay $28.1 million in an out-of-court settlement in the late 1980s.

The state's suit against Morgan Stanley & Co. dragged through the courts for years and the firm finally agreed to pay a $20 million settlement after the state Supreme Court sent the case back to a lower court for retrial in October.
The Chase payment will bring the total amount recovered in the settlements to about $55 million. None of the brokerage firms admitted wrongdoing.
